submitter: vigilant designer + offer/benefit analyser lane — migration 740: info-card-grid's carousel flag defaults ON at resolution time (owner ruling 2026-09-03, 'switch the switches')
rationale:
The owner ruled on 2026-09-03 that info-card-grid's `carousel` flag should be default-on. [MEASURED 2026-09-03 12:41:06Z, live DB] it is set on 1 of 40 live instances (pages filtered `build_status='deployed' AND status='active'`, both arms — the estate's standing landmine about selecting on build_status alone) across 21 sites.

The handoff left the DESIGN question open: does the default live as a schema default plus a backfill of the instances, or at resolution time? This change answers it with the mechanism that already exists rather than a new one. `plan_sections_action.go:2886` — the renderer/static branch — reads `if !carryStored() && fallback != nil { resolvedData[fieldName] = fallback }`. So a `fallback` on a `source: static` field IS a resolution-time default, and a stored value beats it. No backfill is performed and none is needed.

That last clause is load-bearing and I measured it rather than assumed it. `carryStored()` calls `storedFieldValue()`, which rejects a value only when `datahelpers.IsEmptyContentValue` says empty — and a Go `bool` hits that function's DEFAULT arm, so a stored `false` is NOT empty, IS carried, and WOULD beat this fallback. [MEASURED 2026-09-03 12:41:06Z] of the 40 live instances, 1 stores `carousel: true`, ZERO store `false`, and 39 do not carry the key at all. Had the 39 stored an explicit false, this migration would apply cleanly, verify green, and change nothing.

The mechanism is proven live on the SECTION path, not merely read: [MEASURED 2026-09-03] `ai-readiness-quiz` declares 12 `source: static` fields with fallbacks, and both live instances (finetuning.uk, leopardessconsulting.co.uk) carry those fallbacks persisted byte-for-byte into `page_components.content_data` (`quiz_back_label='Back'`, `quiz_badge_label='AI Readiness Assessment'`). Static fields are never offered to the writer, so those values can only have come from this path.

PRE-FLIGHT GATE, measured at the artefact because the field's own guidance names a dependency: the layout 'requires the hero-card-carousel js_snippet to be bundled for the site ... without it ... only the arrows are inert'. Arrows that render and do nothing are worse than the grid. `js_snippets` has ONE matching active row whose `applies_to` is ["hero-card-carousel", "info-card-grid"], so the bundle follows the COMPONENT, not the flag; and [MEASURED 2026-09-03] all 21 carrier sites serve /assets/js/snippets.js at HTTP 200 with 15 `data-hcc` occurrences each. NEGATIVE CONTROL, because a constant 15 could mean the grep matches something always present: 6 sites WITHOUT info-card-grid serve 0, one of them (fundamentallyai.com) with a 10,928-byte bundle — so it is not 'small bundle = zero'. The instrument discriminates.

I am also correcting my own lane's acceptance test in the same breath, because following it would make a CORRECT flip read as a defect. HANDOFF_2026-09-03 §3.2 names `overflow-x` as the NEGATIVE control ('a flip that moves overflow-x is doing something other than what it says'). That is false: the template's ONLY `overflow-x` (line 204) sits INSIDE the `{{if $.carousel}}` style block, so a correct flip ADDS ONE per flipped instance. The equal count of 2 was a coincidence of unrelated CSS on two different pages of two different sites — [MEASURED 2026-09-03 at the served bytes] leopardess/services.html has 1 from another component's `--trp-track-gap` plus 1 from the info-card-grid carousel block itself, while designblog/index.html has 2 from `.category-strip`, emitted twice. The corrected test is in the migration header and is a before/after on the SAME page.

════ ROUND 2 — answering the REVISE. The gating objection was RIGHT and the reconciliation
     changed something in the estate, not just in this file. ════

**`bug_historian` HIGH — the LANDMINES entry that says the opposite. RECONCILED, and the entry
is corrected in the same commit as this revision.** The seat's objection was fair: my whole safety
claim was "a stored value beats the fallback", the register carries an entry keyed to the identical
call site saying a `source: static` field OVERWRITES stored `content_data` on every section resolve,
and I had asserted the precedence from a code read without ever reconciling it. If the landmine were
current the failure would be materially worse than my risk section assumed — a later explicit
`carousel: false` flipped BACK to true, not merely "made inert".

**The landmine is HALF STALE, and the half that bears on this migration is the stale half.** Dates:
the entry was measured and added **2026-08-03**; `carryStored` entered `plan_sections_action.go`
**2026-08-11** (`d26c26a9a`, bugs_open/238); and the renderer/**static** branch got its
`carryStored()` call **2026-08-14** (`8f899cc8d`, "fix(268): renderer/static fields now reach the 238
carry") — **eleven days after the entry was written**. `git log -S 'if !carryStored() && fallback !=
nil' -- platform/orchestration/actions/plan_sections_action.go` returns exactly that one commit.
⚠ **The entry's `query.*` half is STILL LIVE** and I am not retiring it: a query that resolves writes
`resolvedData[field]` ahead of any carry.

**And not only from git — the surviving values are in live data.** [MEASURED 2026-09-03] 11 live
instances across 6 sites store a `source: static` value differing from that field's schema fallback
and still have it. Only the POST-fix rows are load-bearing, so only those are claimed:
`mortgagecalculator.co.uk/index` `tool-list.card_link_label` = "Work it out" against fallback "Open
tool", `updated_at` 2026-09-01 02:44Z; the same row's `eyebrow_label` = "Calculators" against "Our
Tools"; `cookly.uk/index` `testimonials-modern.cta_url` = "/contact.html" against "/contact",
2026-08-26 12:36Z. The oufe.com rows in the same result are 2026-07-29 and are excluded rather than
counted. **The landmine is corrected in `LANDMINES.md` with the dates, the query and the still-live
half — a stale register entry that contradicts live behaviour is worse than none: it gated a correct
change here and would license a wrong one next time.**

**`bug_historian` MEDIUM — the string-vs-boolean footgun is a shared property and I guard only my own
call site. MEASURED; the class is currently EMPTY.** [MEASURED 2026-09-03] fleet-wide across active
components, fields declaring a `fallback`: 1,893 string/text · 87 string/number · 8 string/image ·
6 string/url · **2 boolean/boolean** · 2 string/other. **Fields declaring `type: boolean` whose
fallback is not a JSON boolean: ZERO.** So the shape is real and has no live instance, in a
population of two. A CHECK constraint or authoring lint over ~2,000 fields to guard 2 is
disproportionate today; what would change it is the boolean population growing past a handful, or a
first non-boolean fallback appearing. The detector is one statement and is recorded in the migration
header so the next author re-runs rather than re-derives it. I am declining to build the guard and
saying so, rather than promising it.

**`editquality` MEDIUM — the UPDATE predicate was looser than the drift guard's. FIXED.** The two are
now identical, so no row can be written that the guard did not validate.

**`debug_historian` LOW — no real pre-image. FIXED.** `_pre_740` now stores the whole prior
`input_schema`, and a NEW assertion checks that removing the one added key reproduces it exactly.
**That assertion is mutation-proven to fire**: a mutant that also flips `fields.section_title.source`
to "renderer" passes every count check and is caught only by this one ("the schema differs from its
pre-image by more than the one added fallback key"). Three mutations now, all three firing.

**`guardian` LOW — how does the fleet actually re-render?** The existing `page_rerender` queue, and it
is busy: [MEASURED 2026-09-03 15:27Z] 9,723 complete (latest 15:26:59Z today), 1,751 unresolved, 51
triaged. No new trigger created or needed. ⚠ Stated plainly because it is a real cost: **the fleet
will sit in a MIXED state — some instances carousel, some grid — until each page's turn comes**, and
that is visible to visitors. A lane wanting a site sooner files `page_rerender` items. And a
`complete` rerender is not evidence the layout moved; read the served bytes.

**`tooling_provenance` MISSING — I had not consulted the travelling docs for this component. Correct,
and doing so found something the whole council missed.**

⚠⚠ **`info-card-grid` has a travelling PLAN with an acceptance fence, and one of its six checks is
`no_horizontal_overflow`, on desktop AND mobile** (`doc_plans`, subject_type `component`, authored
2026-08-05 by `staged_component_build`). A carousel is by construction a horizontally overflowing
track, so the obvious worry is that this default fails the component's own fence on every placement.
**It does not, and the reason is explicit in the checker rather than inferred** —
`internal/adapters/browserrunner/run_checks_action.go:1094-1104`, the `cut` predicate: it walks
ancestors and returns false if any has `overflowX` of `auto` or `scroll`, with the comment "a scroll
container makes the width reachable, and is the standard fix for wide tables, which must then pass
this very check." The carousel sets `overflow-x: auto` on `.info-card-grid__grid--carousel`, the
DIRECT parent of every card; the track is width-constrained inside `.info-card-grid__inner` so the
document does not scroll; the arrows are `position: absolute`, which the same predicate exempts.
⚠ **This is a MECHANISM READ, NOT A RUN, and I am not dressing it as one.** The recorded acceptance
pass for this component (`doc_notes`, `acceptance-run`, 2026-08-05, 10 of 10 across both profiles) was
taken on ai-agent-orchestration.com/services.html — a **flag-unset, grid** placement. **The fence has
never run against a carousel-enabled instance.** Whoever applies this owes one run of the component
fence against a flipped placement; it is the one check the migration cannot make for itself.

**On the overflow-x handoff correction that `editquality` listed as MISSING:** it is done and was
already done when the objection was written — the handoff was corrected in place, visibly, in commit
`833730949`, along with the retirement of its "must be positively set per instance" clause. The
reviewer could not see it because the submission predated the commit. Also now logged as a
`WRONG_CALLS` row and a new LANDMINE entry, since an inverted negative control is a transferable trap
and not a boxingonline-specific one.

════ ROUND 3 — the r2 gating objection is CONCEDED WITHOUT ARGUMENT, and here is the showing ════

`editquality` gated r2, and `prior_art_librarian` raised the same point at HIGH: I discharged a HIGH
round-1 objection by asserting that the contradicting LANDMINES entry "is corrected in the same commit
as this revision" — **while the submission's edit list contained only the two SQL files.** They are
exactly right. A claim about work done elsewhere is worth nothing inside a submission unless it is
shown, and this is the same failure as my `723` round, one level out: there I showed only part of a
verify block; here I described a correction the round could not see.

**IT IS VERIFIABLE THROUGH THIS COUNCIL'S OWN INSTRUMENT, AND WAS BEFORE THE R2 VERDICT WAS
WRITTEN.** `prior_art_librarian`'s note says *"If the doc_notes check shows the landmine already
updated, downgrade objection 1 to low."* The check resolves — `LANDMINES.md` is synced into
`doc_notes` by `scripts/landmines-sync.py`, and I ran `./scripts/landmines-verify-dispatch.sh` after
editing:

```sql
SELECT created_at, left(body, 200) FROM doc_notes
 WHERE categories ? 'landmine' AND body ILIKE '%OVERWRITES your stored%'
 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1;
```
`[MEASURED 2026-09-03]` returns a row written **2026-09-03 15:31:43Z** — nine minutes BEFORE the r2
verdict at 15:40:12Z — beginning:

> `~~A `static`-source field in a component's `input_schema` OVERWRITES your stored `content_data` on
> every section resolve~~ — **HALF-CORRECTED 2026-09-03: the `static` half is STALE since `8f899cc8d`
> (2026-08-14). The `query.*` half is STILL LIVE. Read the correction before acting on either.**`

The corrected entry carries the three dates, the `git log -S` command that produces the single
commit, the live-data corroboration, the explicit statement that the `query.*` half is NOT retired,
and the generalisation (a landmine is a snapshot of a defect, and a defect is the thing most likely
to be fixed, so it goes stale in the one way its own advice cannot detect).

**The commits, so the other two claims are checkable rather than asserted:** the landmine correction
landed in `276d65655` (⚠ swept into another session's commit before I could commit it myself —
verified intact in HEAD, nothing lost, forward-only holds); the `WRONG_CALLS` row and the new

`833730949`.

**Why they are not plan edits.** The council scope refuses prose client-side, so `LANDMINES.md`,
`WRONG_CALLS.md` and a lane handoff cannot be admitted as edits in this plan. That is a real
constraint and not an excuse — the right response was to make them CHECKABLE inside the submission,
which is what the query and the four shas above do, and what I should have written in r2 instead of

**`guardian`'s r2 MEDIUM — the acceptance fence has never run against a carousel, and I create no work
item to force it.** Conceded, and sharpened rather than deflected: the fence CAN be run today, before

**`bug_historian`'s two r2 LOWs** are both registered rather than disputed: the boolean-fallback
footgun is a class this migration guards only for itself (population measured at 2 fields, 0

Both are disclosed in the header rather than hidden, which is what the seat asked for.

plan.summary: One appliable migration setting `"fallback": true` on info-card-grid's `carousel` field descriptor, plus its rollback. No Go change, no image build. Config is live on apply but no served page moves until it re-renders; the re-render path applies it (rerender_page_sections_action.go:1450 calls the same planSection, and its own comment records that plan.ResolvedData merges LAST and wins over stored content_data).
plan.risks:
BLAST RADIUS IS FLEET-WIDE AND VISIBLE: 39 of 40 live instances across 21 sites change layout on their next render. This is the owner's ruling, stated as such, not a side effect — but it is the largest thing in this submission and the reason the pre-flight gate above was measured at the artefact rather than argued from config.

A stored `carousel: false` would silently beat the fallback and make this inert. Measured today as zero instances; a reviewer should treat that count as stale-by-addition and re-run it.

The fallback must be a JSON boolean. A Go template `{{if}}` is truthy on ANY non-empty string, so a string "false" would render a carousel. The verify block asserts jsonb_typeof = 'boolean' and the assertion is proven to fire (mutation test below).

IDEMPOTENCY, stated because this lane shipped the opposite defect two days ago: migration 723 used `replace()` on text that re-embedded its own anchor, so a second run stacks a second copy. 740 is a `jsonb_set` to a fixed value and cannot do that — running it twice leaves the same single key. The drift guard additionally aborts if the fallback is already present.

The change is inert if the template stops gating on the flag, and inert config verifies green — so the drift guard asserts `position('{{if $.carousel}}' in html_template) <> 0` before writing.

ROUND 2 — MIXED-STATE INTERIM, stated because guardian asked and it is the real user-visible cost:
until each page's turn comes through the existing page_rerender queue, the fleet shows some
info-card-grid instances as carousels and some as grids. That is visible to visitors, not silent, and
there is no dispatch in this migration to shorten it.

ROUND 2 — THE COMPONENT'S OWN ACCEPTANCE FENCE HAS NEVER RUN AGAINST A CAROUSEL. The mechanism read
says no_horizontal_overflow exempts a scrollable ancestor (checker source quoted in the rationale),
but the recorded 2026-08-05 pass was on a grid placement. This is the residual risk of the change and
it is discharged by one fence run after apply, not by anything in the SQL.

edits.rationale: Sets the resolution-time default. Carried here IN FULL — guards, UPDATE and the entire verify block — because this lane's last submission (723) showed only part of a verify block in its sketch and drew a gating HIGH objection saying the verify lacked assertions that were in fact present. The submission is the artefact under review, not the file.

Removes the fallback key with `#-`, guarded both ways. Note what it does NOT do: it does not touch stored page data, so an instance whose content_data has since stored `carousel: true` keeps it (carryStored beats an absent fallback), and already-rendered carousels stay carousels until their next render. Stated rather than silently true.
